name: Collotype
summary: A way to print a photograph from a plate of hardened gelatin. The print has continuous tone, with a fine reticulation and no screen.
how: Coat a glass plate with gelatin and expose it under a negative; the gelatin hardens in proportion to the light.
Wet the plate; the soft gelatin takes water and rejects ink, and the hard gelatin takes ink.
Print a run of up to about 1,000 sheets, because the gelatin wears.
Print in one black or brown, or in a set of three to six plates for colour.

origin.note: Alphonse Poitevin invented and patented the process in 1855.

adoptions.via: Joseph Albert and Jakub Husník make a gelatin plate on glass, and Albert builds the first mechanised collotype press.
Eadweard Muybridge publishes Animal Locomotion with 781 plates printed as collotypes.
